title: Lucky
series: Lucky, a scrolly essay on the Talent vs Luck model
style: a lab notebook on graph paper: people are black ink blots, luck is glossy green and red ink balls, Fraunces display type, a yellow highlighter
context: The video explains the Talent vs Luck agent-based model by Alessandro Pluchino, Alessio Emanuele Biondo and Andrea Rapisarda (Advances in Complex Systems 21, 2018; arXiv:1802.07068; 2022 Ig Nobel Prize in Economics). 1,000 agents with talent ~ Normal(0.6, 0.1) sit still on a 201×201 torus, all starting with 10 units of capital. 500 events (half lucky, half unlucky) random-walk 2 patches every six months for 80 steps (40 years). A lucky event within 1 patch doubles capital with probability equal to talent; an unlucky one halves it. Results: wealth follows a power law (top 20% hold ~80%); in the paper's single run the richest had talent 0.61 (capital 2,560), the most talented (0.89) ended with 0.625; over 10,000 runs the richest person's talent averages 0.667 ± 0.09; only 32% of talented people (T > 0.7) end above their starting capital. Funding: giving everyone 1 unit every 5 years raised that share to 69.48%; giving to the most successful added under 20 points; random funding of 25% added 35.95 points. The authors' NetLogo code is on CoMSES. Related: Robert H. Frank, Success and Luck (2016).
